exposure: bacterial etiologic agents (Coagulase-negative staphylococci, Klebsiella spp., Escherichia coli)
cohort: 197 infants diagnosed with culture-proven sepsis, including 40% premature births, in a tertiary neonatal intensive care unit.
finding: Neonatal sepsis continues to have high mortality rates (10%) in tertiary NICUs, with Coagulase-negative staphylococci being the most common etiologic agent overall and Klebsiella spp. being the most common Gram-negative agent in late-onset sepsis.
